newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's BKME to shed 49pct of subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's BKME to shed 49pct of subsidiary.

text.p: The Bank of Kuwait & the Middle East (BKME) plans to sell 49 percent of its fully-owned Kuwait & the Middle East Financial Investment Company, a bank official said on Tuesday.

"Of the 49 million shares earmarked for the sale 23.27 million will be put for a shareholders' subscription, an equal amount will be sold in a public auction and 2.45 million will be sold to the company staff," the official said.
The sale is expected to earn BKME about 10-12 million dinars. BKME reported a net profit rise of 112.9 percent to 5.752 million dinars.

A banking source said the sale was advised by the central bank which prefers that banks do not fully own investment firms. State institutions own 58 percent of BKME, the rest belongs to private investors.
The share price for the subscription, tentatively set for June 8-10, was fixed at 200 fils a share, which will also be the starting price for the auction planned for May 29.
Private investors "have made offers for a bigger price," said the official. The par value of the share is 100 fils. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
Only shareholders registered on May 28th will be eligible for the offering. If the subscription was not fully covered the remaining shares could be at the open market, he added.

The bank will address the Kuwait Stock Exchange in the coming days to list the company's share, the official said. KSE regulations term that a firm should have a shareholder base of no less than 100 investors to be listed on the bourse.
The company, which is not obliged to announce its results being a private firm, is believed to have made a net profit rise of more than 100 percent to about one million dinars in 1996.
Official figures about the company's performance are expected to be released ahead of the sale.
The company carries out local and global investment activities for own and others.
Only nationals of Kuwait and fellow Gulf Arab states -- The United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain -- can trade in Kuwait shares.
